To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the topology of a gene correlation network is a useful source of information for the identification of gene sets that are enriched for genes that are differentially expressed in a particular phenotype.

(i) the topology of the correlation network influences the identification of functional modules that are associated with phenotypic differences, (ii) the influence is not limited to modules that are directly connected to the phenotype, but extends to modules that are connected to the phenotype through other modules, and (iii) the influence of the topology is not restricted to modules that are associated positively or negatively with the phenotype, but also extends to modules that have no direct association with the phenotype.

the topology of a gene network can be used to identify functionally coherent modules that correlate with a phenotypic change, and that these modules are significantly different between the two phenotypes.

a novel way of identifying functional modules that correlate strongly with phenotypic differences.
the problem of relating observed phenotypically altered states of a system to the collective changes of genes.
the identification of functional modules that are associated with phenotypic differences.

we have developed a method for identifying the functional modules that are most strongly correlated with a particular phenotypic difference, and we have shown that these modules are strongly influenced by the topology of the correlation network.

we have developed a novel method for the identification of functional modules that are significantly correlated with phenotypic change, and that we have applied this method to the problem of identifying functional modules that are associated with the development of resistance to chemotherapy.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the topology of a gene correlation network can have a significant effect on the outcome of a gene set enrichment analysis, and that this effect can be substantial enough to reverse the direction of the analysis, and to identify a different set of genes.
network topology can have a substantial influence on the identification of functional modules that distinguish phenotypes.

the inclusion of network topology in gene set enrichment analysis can substantially alter the interpretation of gene expression data, and that the resulting alterations in gene set interpretation are likely to be important in understanding the underlying biology.
